question.text: Under the new tax regime effective from FY 2024-25, which of the following deductions is still available to an individual assessee?

answer.text: Deduction under Section 80C for PPF, ELSS, and life insurance premiums
Deduction under Section 80D for health insurance premiums
Deduction under Section 80CCD(2) for employer's contribution to NPS
Deduction under Section 80TTA for savings bank interest

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the new tax regime, most Chapter VI-A deductions are disallowed. However, Section 80CCD(2) for employer's contribution to NPS remains available. Under the current source pages, the new-regime limit for non-government/private employees is up to 14% of salary. Sections 80C, 80D, and 80TTA are NOT available under the new regime. The Trap: Section 80C is the most commonly claimed deduction and candidates may assume it continues under the new regime. Section 80D for health insurance is also commonly used but is unavailable. Section 80TTA interest deduction is similarly disallowed. Note: NISM Series X-B workbook (pages 147, 166, 270) confirms Section 80CCD(2) employer NPS contribution remains available under the new regime, with the new-regime limit for private/other employees at 14% of salary.
